jess (AE): Heads up — AcmeCorp POC wants Private deployment behind their on‑prem firewall. They need guidance: PrivateLink vs TGW peering, how to preserve client IP for logs, and any ports/rules + pricing impact. Can we align on ask?
ben (NetOps): Quick Q — is this ‘customer-initiated’ egress to our service (i.e., they will open outbound to our infra) or do they expect our service to call into their network?
maria (SE): They said outbound from customer to Redwood Private control/data plane. Wants no internet egress (tight firewall), so likely interface endpoint or VPN to our VPC.
sam (Sales Eng): Pricing note: Private (on‑prem/VPC) = platform license + infra run rate. If they want dedicated capacity, add reserved commit. I'll ping pricing if they pick PrivateLink-only.
jess (AE): Confirmed: customer prefers PrivateLink/Interface endpoints to avoid egress over public internet. Wants source IP preserved in logs and SNI passthrough so their TLS proxy can still inspect traffic.
ben (NetOps): Two things to call out: 1) with AWS Interface VPC Endpoints, the traffic terminates at the endpoint ENI in the service VPC — from their app point-of-view you see the ENI as the target, so original client source IP is not preserved across NAT unless we run a proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For. 2) If they need raw client IP at the backend, we usually recommend a TCP proxy that preserves srcIP only if the proxy runs in their network (or use a BGP/NAT trick).
maria (SE): Short configuration sketch for a typical setup (customer->PrivateLink->Redwood):
```
# Security Group on customer side (allow outbound to endpoint)
Type: TLS  Protocol: TCP   Port: 443   Destination: com-redwood-internal-endpoint-ENIs (CIDR or endpoint IPs)
# On their perimeter FW: allow outbound 443 SNI to our endpoint FQDN/IPs
```
Note: since TLS is terminated by Redwood service, we can surface client addr in headers: `x-forwarded-for` (app must trust header).
ben (NetOps): If customer insists on TLS inspection in the middle (MITM proxy), SNI will be readable by the proxy only if the TLS handshake is unmodified. If they do TLS intercept, it breaks end-to-end TLS and our cert pinning/mTLS options. Recommend either: (A) TLS passthrough (no inspect) or (B) install a company CA + allow our cert chain to be trusted — smells like enterprise blocker.
sam (Sales Eng): For pricing/ops: if they force TLS intercept, we may need a dedicated proxy in their VPC (Redwood-managed or customer-managed) — additional infra/setup fee and a higher support tier.
jess (AE): Customer also asked about egress IPs for firewall allowlist (they prefer static IPs).
maria (SE): We can provide one of these patterns: 1) PrivateLink with fixed endpoint ENI IPs (not globally static) — customer can allow endpoint CIDRs or security group. 2) Use a NAT EIP + proxy in their VPC to preserve a single egress IP. 3) Recommend TGW/Transit + route to a small outbound proxy (gives predictable EIP). Each has tradeoffs on preserve-srcip and cost.
ben (NetOps): Example firewall snippet for allowlist (if they accept endpoint CIDRs):
```
FW rule: ALLOW TCP 443 -> 10.1.23.0/27  # interface endpoint ENIs (sample CIDR)
FW note: allow ephemeral return ports if stateful; if stateful firewall then only 443 outbound is fine.
```
jess (AE): Action items: can someone draft a one-page options doc we can send to customer with recommended path + cost delta and clear blocker callouts? (SNI inspect = big blocker).
maria (SE): I’ll draft the options doc. Quick TL;DR to include: PrivateLink = lowest ops, may require X-Forwarded-For for client IP. TGW/peering + outbound proxy = predictable EIP + src IP preservation (more customer ops). Dedicated Reserved = better latency/cost at scale. TLS intercept forces on‑prem proxy or trust changes — escalate with security team.
sam (Sales Eng): tagging pricing: if they want a Redwood‑managed proxy in their VPC add one‑time setup + $X/mo (will confirm), otherwise customer‑managed proxy is no extra Redwood infra charge.
infra-bot: Deploy note — if customer opts for a Redwood-managed proxy we need: `vpc-id, subnet-ids, route-table-ids, security-group-ids, allowed-admin-cidrs` before schedule.
jess (AE): Great. @maria please drop the doc here when ready and @sam loop pricing. Also adding a short sample checklist for their network ops to avoid back-and-forth.
maria (SE): Will post doc + checklist in 2 hours.
sam (Sales Eng): I’ll attach a pricing sketch once Maria posts. :thumbsup:
